Verifier notes and special checks

The first bar prints the treble and bass clefs, the three flats, and 2/4. Later systems reprint those clefs and the three flats; the clef in force does not change. There is no pickup, repeat, ending, or meter change. The tenth, twelfth, twentieth, and twenty-second bars are narrow and still complete. The last bar closes with a thin stroke and a thick stroke. The title and the publisher line sit outside the system crops; the tempo, slurs, dynamics, and pedal marks stay inside.

  • System 5, right end of the last bar: Does the thick stroke after the thin stroke start another bar, or close this one? It closes the bar. The thin stroke at crop x 1512 runs through both staves, and the thick stroke at crop x 1517-1523 stands immediately beside it. No repeat dots are printed.
  • System 5, between the left barline and the next barline: Is the vertical stroke near crop x 419 a barline? No. It is a note stem. It does not run through both staves the way the barline at crop x 516 does.
  • Systems 3 and 5, the narrow bars: Are the narrow bars pickups or incomplete bars? No. Each has its own left and right barline through both staves, and the printed notes fill two quarter-note beats: two quarter chords, or a half note.
  • Each system end: Does any system end without a barline, so that its last bar continues on the next system? No. Systems 1 through 4 end with a single barline through both staves, and system 5 ends with the thin-and-thick final barline.
  • Page above system 1 and below system 5: Is musical ink left outside the system crops?
